title: Enforce production-ready closure gates
summary: Update gateway and roadmap closure policy so code-changing tasks and sprints cannot close unless TDD code tests, linters, validation, and task-scoped ship-ready quality pass.

goal.outcome: Task-close, sprint-close, and ship-ready gates enforce production-ready semantics for code-changing work and preserve publication/release as separate explicit approval boundaries.
acceptance: Gateway preflight blocks code-changing task-close when executable code tests are missing, failed, or not mapped to the implementation build.
Gateway preflight blocks task-close when required linters or validation evidence are missing for the changed scope.
Task-close requires task-scoped ship-ready validation for the exact changed content before roadmap status can become `done`.
Sprint-close requires all sprint tasks to be task-done or explicitly cancelled, shared outcome/risk reconciliation, and ship-ready quality when the sprint changes shippable code/package behavior.
Ship-ready validates exact content candidate quality but does not imply publication, release, push, remote update, or destructive action approval.
Gateway/report terminology favors gate, linter, test, validation, and evidence while preserving required compatibility fields.
Roadmap close/cancel behavior reports the smallest safe next loop when production-ready criteria are missing.
non_goals: Do not publish, push, release, or perform destructive actions.
Do not remove existing validation report compatibility fields before migration coverage exists.
Do not require executable code tests for docs-only or mechanical changes unless policy says behavior changed.
Do not bypass fresh validation/context requirements for high-risk or ship-ready gates.
verification: wiki_gate/task-close linters for alignment, changed, task, generated-parity, and source-contract
